name: Arousing the thought of awakening (bodhicittotpāda)
method_summary: Resolving to attain full buddhahood for the sake of all beings — the entry into the bodhisattva path, renewed throughout it; the Larger Sukhāvatīvyūha requires it even of the lowest aspirants.

name: Taking the bodhisattva vows (praṇidhāna)
method_summary: Formulating vows for beings' welfare — Śrīmālā's ten vows and three aspirations, the Avataṃsaka's vows attached to every daily act, the great vows of Samantabhadra.

name: Practice of the six perfections
method_summary: Giving, morality, patience, vigor, meditation and wisdom practiced together, each 'perfected' by the perfection of wisdom (not apprehending giver, gift or recipient).

name: Giving without support
method_summary: Giving without resting on the notion of any object, sign, giver or recipient; its merit is immeasurable like space.

name: Patience (kṣānti) without the notion of self
method_summary: Bearing harm without anger by not holding the notions of self, being, soul or person (the Kaliṅga story); bowing to all as future buddhas even when abused (Sadāparibhūta).

name: Abstaining from meat (Mahāyāna)
method_summary: Not eating meat, fish or (in some texts) the five pungent plants, out of compassion for beings seen as one's relatives in past lives; prescribed by the Laṅkāvatāra (ch. 8), the Mahāparinirvāṇa and the Brahmajāla precepts.
notes: Not required in the Pali Vinaya (see dsp:is-meat-eating-permitted); Tibetan practice varies.

name: Receiving the Brahmajāla bodhisattva precepts
method_summary: Receiving the ten major and forty-eight minor precepts, open to lay and ordained, and reciting them fortnightly; in Japanese Tendai (Saichō) the sole ordination precepts.

name: Seeking and serving the spiritual friend
method_summary: Seeking out good friends without weariness and honoring them — Sudhana's pilgrimage and Sadāprarudita's sacrifice are the models; the buddhas and perfections are the bodhisattva's true friends.

warnings.text: New bodhisattvas in the hands of bad friends become frightened of the profound teaching.

name: Reciting, memorizing and teaching sūtras
method_summary: Taking up, keeping, reading, reciting, explaining and teaching a sūtra or even one four-line verse of it.

name: Copying and honoring sūtras
method_summary: Writing out the sūtra and honoring the book with flowers, incense, banners and parasols; the book is kept as a shrine.

name: The five practices of the dharma-teacher (Lotus)
method_summary: Receiving and keeping, reading, reciting, explaining and copying the Lotus Sūtra.

name: Preaching the dharma (dharmabhāṇaka practice)
method_summary: Teaching the sūtra seated on the Tathāgata's seat (emptiness), wearing his robe (patience), in his room (compassion); the four peaceful practices for the latter age.

name: The sevenfold (seven-branch) worship
method_summary: Homage, offering, confession, rejoicing, requesting the teaching, requesting the buddhas to remain, dedication — from the Bhadracarī; the frame of Tibetan and Newar liturgies.

name: Reciting Samantabhadra's ten great vows
method_summary: Recitation and practice of the ten vows of the 40-fascicle Avataṃsaka, dedicated to birth in Sukhāvatī.

name: Dedicating merit (pariṇāmanā)
method_summary: Turning all merit toward awakening for all beings, ideally without apprehending merit, dedicator or goal.

warnings.text: Dedication made with apprehension of signs is 'poisoned, with a thorn'.

name: Rejoicing in merit (anumodanā)
method_summary: Rejoicing in the good deeds of buddhas, bodhisattvas and all beings.

name: Confession before the thirty-five buddhas
method_summary: Reciting the names of the thirty-five buddhas with prostrations, confessing wrongs, rejoicing and dedicating.

name: The Golden Light confession
method_summary: Confessing all evil done in ignorance before the buddhas, as heard from the golden drum; rejoicing and dedication; used in East Asian repentance rites.

name: Lotus repentance and Samantabhadra visualization
method_summary: Repentance of the six senses before Samantabhadra, reciting the Lotus, contemplating the true mark; Samantabhadra appears on his white elephant to the reciter.
notes: Tiantai's 'Lotus samādhi' ritual (Zhiyi) belongs to U54.

name: Calling on the name of Avalokiteśvara
method_summary: Single-mindedly calling the bodhisattva's name in danger or need (Lotus 25).

name: Recitation of oṃ maṇipadme hūṃ
method_summary: Recollecting and reciting Avalokiteśvara's six-syllable great vidyā.
notes: Tibetan practice lineages (maṇi recitation, nyungne) are for the Tibetan units.

name: Reciting the Heart Sūtra and its mantra
method_summary: Recitation of the Heart Sūtra and 'gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā', daily in East Asian monasteries and, in Tibet, to avert obstacles.

name: Dhāraṇī recitation
method_summary: Reciting protective dhāraṇīs given in the sūtras (Lotus 26; the Great Compassion and Uṣṇīṣavijayā dhāraṇīs).

name: The Śūraṅgama mantra
method_summary: Reciting the long Śūraṅgama mantra (in Chinese monasteries in the morning service); the sūtra's altar-rite for the latter age.

name: Bhaiṣajyaguru rites for the sick and dying
method_summary: Keeping the Medicine Buddha's name, reciting the sūtra, lighting lamps and hanging banners to prolong life and heal.
notes: The number of lamps and days of the rite are given in the Chinese versions; not recorded here.

name: Kṣitigarbha recitation and offerings for the dead
method_summary: Reciting Kṣitigarbha's name and sūtra and making offerings during the forty-nine days after a death.

name: Offering the body or its parts by fire (Lotus 23)
method_summary: The Lotus's Bhaiṣajyarāja chapter praises a past bodhisattva who burned his body as an offering and says burning a finger or toe at a stūpa exceeds offering kingdoms; East Asian ordination customs of burning incense marks derive from it. Summary only.

warnings.text: The same chapter ranks keeping even one four-line verse of the sūtra above all such bodily offerings.
The Vinaya forbids monks and nuns to harm their own bodies or seek death; Chinese critics (e.g. Yijing) opposed such offerings as contrary to the Vinaya.
warnings.ref: (Vinaya rules on self-harm; Yijing's account — from memory, unverified)

name: Coursing in the perfection of wisdom by non-apprehension
method_summary: Not taking hold of form or any dharma, not even of 'bodhisattva', 'perfection of wisdom' or 'nirvāṇa', and not being frightened by this; standing nowhere as the Tathāgata stands.

warnings.text: Beginners hearing this may be frightened; not to be taught to the unprepared (see also Ākāśagarbha's downfall of teaching emptiness to the unready).

name: Seeing the conditioned as a dream (Diamond verse)
method_summary: Contemplating all conditioned dharmas as stars, a fault of vision, a lamp, an illusion, dew, a bubble, a dream, lightning, a cloud.

name: Calm and insight as taught in the Saṃdhinirmocana
method_summary: Calm on images without discrimination, insight on images with discrimination, recognizing the image as cognition only, until both are united.

name: The four dhyānas of the Laṅkāvatāra
method_summary: Meditation on the no-self of persons, on the no-self of dharmas, on suchness, and the Tathāgata's dhyāna.

name: Turning the hearing back (Avalokiteśvara's perfect penetration)
method_summary: Reversing the hearing to hear the self-nature: entering the stream of hearing, forgetting sound and hearing, until the self-nature becomes the supreme way (Śūraṅgama juan 6).

warnings.text: The fifty demonic states arising in meditation are not to be taken as sagehood.

name: Recollection of the Buddha's body and qualities
method_summary: Calling to mind the Tathāgata's golden body, marks and qualities until samādhi, knowing the buddha recollected to be neither form nor formless.

name: The single-practice samādhi (yixing sanmei)
method_summary: Sitting in solitude facing the direction of a buddha and reciting his name continuously until one sees all buddhas in that one and knows the sameness of the dharmadhātu.

name: The samādhi of the buddhas standing before one
method_summary: Recollecting Amitābha single-mindedly (the sūtra: for seven days and nights) until one sees him face to face or in a dream, understanding the vision as made by mind. Tiantai made it the 'constantly walking samādhi' of ninety days; summary only.

warnings.text: The buddhas seen are mind-made and neither come nor go; the vision is not to be grasped as real.

notes: The prolonged forms (sleep and posture restrictions over ninety days) belong to later manuals; no method recorded here.

name: The sixteen contemplations of the Contemplation Sūtra
method_summary: Successive visualizations of the setting sun, water and ice, the jewelled ground, trees, ponds, towers, the lotus throne, the images, Amitāyus' body, the two bodhisattvas, one's own birth there, and the nine grades of birth.

name: Calling the name of Amitābha (nianfo / nembutsu)
method_summary: Thinking of Amitābha and calling 'namo Amitābha Buddha' — ten times even at death (Contemplation Sūtra), holding the name one to seven days with undistracted mind (Smaller Sūtra), with faith in the eighteenth vow (Larger Sūtra).
notes: Sūtra layer; the schools' practice (Shandao, Hōnen, Shinran) is U43.

name: The sick bodhisattva's contemplation
method_summary: When ill, seeing the illness as arising from clinging to 'I' and 'mine', removing the illness but not the dharmas, and extending the insight that all beings' illness is likewise unreal into compassion.
